blindVocabulary.why: Derived from this tree's own call frequencies, not assumed. #expect and #require are deliberately absent from the readers: every swift-testing assertion wraps one, so including them would suppress every finding and turn the pass into a dead predicate. The read has to be the product verb inside the assertion. Swift reads state through parenless computed properties, so the reader list carries dot-prefixed property names as well as call verbs; the first pass without them reported 121 blind where the true figure is far lower, and three of the tests it named read their latch back on the very next line. PRO-0079 measured the pass rather than believing it: 57 of the 78 findings were read (5 per bucket at seed 20260821 across act/unlock/release/set/claim, plus a census of the 32-finding tail) and every one was a false positive — 0 genuine, 95% upper bound 3 in 78. `.calls` and `.recorded` were added on that evidence: they are one idiom in two spellings, the spy double's ledger asserted on after a mutation (`#expect(!h.provider.calls.contains { $0.0 == "stop" })`, `#expect(cloneScript.recorded.contains(["clone", ...]))`), used across 8 test files in 45 places, and they take the count 78 -> 76. Every other candidate was refused with its numbers. `.contains` (93 files, 865 uses) and `.stringValue` (31 files) are assertion plumbing and would behave like #expect by another name; `.inFlight`, `.drawing`, `.armCount`, `.stepsAside`, `.recognisedPids`, `.outstandingCall` are one property on one fake in 1-3 files each and adding them is tuning toward zero. The reader list is not the lever here and adding to it should not be mistaken for fixing the pass: only 15 of the 57 false positives were vocabulary at all. The other 42 are structural — 17 where a mutator prefix-matched a non-mutating identifier (the test's own name in the func line, a pure query like `pauseLimit(`, or an enum case like `.stopRun(` inside the assertion), 10 where the mutator is the subject and the read is on what it returned, 9 read-then-teardown, 4 test doubles counted as tests, 2 where the body ran on into a `private func` the body regex cannot start at. No reader list can reach any of those. An out-of-family reviewer (grok-4.6, xhigh) confirmed the six shapes and the bound and argued `.calls`/`.recorded` should also be refused — not as plumbing, but because two spellings moving the count by 2 does not make the list usable and starts the accretion the refusals above avoid. Recorded here rather than acted on, because the brief asks for the idiom the sample proves; if the count is ever tuned again, that dissent is the argument to read first.
